scenes.heading: Structured Data
scenes.subheading: Data that fits neatly into rows and columns
scenes.narration: Structured data is organized into a fixed schema of rows and columns, making it easy to store and query in relational databases.

scenes.heading: What makes data structured
bullets: A predefined schema with named columns
Consistent data types in every column
Rows that all follow the same shape
scenes.narration: Structured data has a predefined schema, so every column has a known name and meaning. Each column holds a consistent data type, which keeps the data predictable. Every row follows the same shape, so records are uniform. Because of this regularity, structured data is naturally queried with SQL.

scenes.heading: A structured table in SQL
scenes.narration: This table definition captures the essence of structured data: each column has a fixed name and type. The customer_id column is an integer that uniquely identifies each row. Because the schema is enforced, every record must conform to this shape, which is exactly what makes structured data reliable to query.

scenes.heading: Structured vs unstructured
scenes.narration: Structured data has a fixed schema of rows and columns and is queried directly with SQL. Unstructured data, like text or images, has no such schema and needs specialized tools to interpret. The regular shape of structured data is what makes it so convenient for analytics.

scenes.text: Structured data's fixed schema makes it the easiest, most query-friendly form of data.
scenes.narration: The key point is that a fixed schema makes structured data predictable and easy to query, which is why it powers most business reporting.
